solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Colour endless in a divine English novel

indicators.note: the colour loses its last letter
the shortened colour sits inside the divine

parts.note: DD = Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A literary critic muses on the colours in a devout English novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a clergyman, and DD is the degree after his name. Adam Bede is George Eliot's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: George Eliot's first full-length book, published in 1859, is one instance of the category.

clue.text: Help mounted soldiers cutting spring migration

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up turns the word over
the soldiers cut into the spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Mounted troops arrive to help with a seasonal migration in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: "Mounted soldiers" looks like cavalry, but "mounted" belongs to "Help": in a down entry it lifts AID to read DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the scattering or migration of a people from their homeland.

clue.text: Folk performer, crafty poet leading reindeer

parts.note: William Morris, Arts and Crafts designer and poet

explanation.surface: A cunning poet heads a herd of reindeer at a folk festival.
explanation.walkthrough: "Crafty" here means of the Arts and Crafts movement, not cunning: William Morris led it and wrote poetry. A morris dancer performs a traditional English folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A morris dancer performs traditional English folk dances with bells and sticks.

clue.text: Nutty green apple finally prepared for cake

indicators.note: take the last letter of apple
the letters are made ready, rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker prepares green apples and nuts for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: "Nutty green" reads as two adjectives describing an apple; in fact it is a noun phrase, a green who is nuts about the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Green as a noun is an environmentalist, and nutty adds the fanaticism the slang freak carries.

clue.text: Just for Latinists, this with others has to go round

indicators.note: the words are to be put into Latin
the Latin for others surrounds the Latin for this

parts.note: et al, Latin for and others

explanation.surface: A pedantic note on Latin grammar about words that must surround others.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces must be translated into Latin: hic is this and et al. is and others.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and ethical both mean morally right.

clue.text: Complaint NHS department's well able to explain?

parts.note: ENT = ear, nose and throat; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Can the NHS department that handles this complaint explain itself properly?
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. The question mark flags a looser definition: a fluent speaker is well able to explain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluent speaker expresses themselves easily, so is well able to explain.

clue.text: Duke in good health carrying spades

indicators.note: the word for good health holds the spades

explanation.surface: A healthy duke goes about carrying garden spades.
explanation.walkthrough: "Duke" looks like a nobleman, but dukes is slang for fists, as in "put up your dukes".
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist.

clue.text: Plot involving alien laser beam accidentally revealed?

indicators.note: the plot takes in the alien and the beam

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A science-fiction plot in which an alien's laser beam gives something away.
explanation.walkthrough: "Plot" reads as a story line; it is a garden bed. The question mark allows betrayed in its sense of gave away unintentionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayed can mean unintentionally showed, as a blush betrays embarrassment.

clue.text: Maybe 501s with shirt put outside to air

indicators.note: the shirt goes around the jeans

parts.note: 501s are a style of Levi's jeans

explanation.surface: Jeans and a shirt are hung outside to air.
explanation.walkthrough: "To air" sounds like drying laundry; here air means broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Air in the broadcasting sense, as in a programme going out on air, is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Young swimmer Henry's widow

definitions.meaning: a young salmon, before it goes to sea
Henry VIII's sixth wife, Catherine, outlived him

explanation.surface: A young swimmer turns out to be the widow of someone called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII and the only one to survive him.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon; Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's widow.

clue.text: Chilled environment in wild for rare tiger

indicators.note: wild means out of control, and letters out of control will not keep their order

explanation.surface: A zoo keeps a rare tiger in a cool enclosure in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: "Environment" suggests a habitat for the tiger; the chilled environment is simply a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description rather than a synonym: the fridge is literally a cold space that surrounds whatever is kept in it.

clue.text: Fools in America delinquent once hit

parts.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s young tearaway

explanation.surface: A news item about foolish American young offenders who once struck someone.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fools" is plural, so two ASSes. A Ted was a Teddy boy, a British youth of the 1950s in Edwardian-style dress, a byword for delinquency, hence "once".
explanation.definitionFit: A mob hit is a killing, so hit means assassinated.

clue.text: Dessert timid sort swallows slowly at first

indicators.note: the timid sort takes the letter inside
take the first letter of slowly

explanation.surface: A shy diner eats pudding slowly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a shy person a mouse is the usual crossword shorthand for timid sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the light whipped chocolate or fruit pudding is one kind of sweet course.

clue.text: Blakey for one is to strive for creative skill

explanation.surface: A musician named Blakey works hard at his craft.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Blakey was an American jazz drummer; British readers may also think of Blakey from the sitcom On the Buses, but only Art works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names the skill an artist brings to the work.

clue.text: Nothing stops Kelvin, a debauchee, in pub activity

indicators.note: the nothing plugs the gap inside the debauchee

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: Nothing can halt Kelvin, a hard-living man, when he gets going at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: "Kelvin" reads as a man's name, but it is the temperature unit, K.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke, singing along to backing tracks, is a common pub activity.

clue.text: Almost do away with range of knowledge on New York City

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end

explanation.surface: An attempt to wipe out the sum of knowledge about New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: "New York City" looks like one unit; the definition is City alone, and Kilkenny is a city in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilkenny is a city in the south-east of Ireland.

clue.text: Adult struck — struck with shame

explanation.surface: An adult is hit, and then feels thoroughly ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated "struck" does two jobs: first a physical blow, then the start of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means disconcerted and embarrassed, the feeling of being hit by shame.

clue.text: Bishop in argument about new Victorian poet

indicators.note: the bishop comes in at the front of the argument
the argument goes round the new

explanation.surface: A bishop is caught up in a dispute about a new Victorian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowing, rhyming with cow, is British for having a row. Robert Browning was a leading Victorian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning was one of the great Victorian poets.

clue.text: Place abnormally loaded with hidden gold

indicators.note: the letters are arranged abnormally
the gold is concealed inside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A place unusually rich, stuffed with buried gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the legendary city, rich with gold. OR as gold comes from heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary place of gold sought by explorers in South America.

clue.text: Shock where old hand guzzles gallon

indicators.note: the old hand swallows the gallon

parts.note: an old stager is a veteran

explanation.surface: It's shocking how much an old man can drink.
explanation.walkthrough: "Old hand" is one unit: an old stager, a veteran. Stagger means shock or astound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: news that makes you reel astonishes you.

clue.text: Jousting weapon returned to lake for knight

indicators.note: turns 'to lake' back to front

explanation.surface: A knight's jousting lance is returned to the lake, as Excalibur was.
explanation.walkthrough: "Returned" looks as if it acts on the weapon, as Excalibur was returned to the lake, but it acts on what follows. Fittingly, the knight was known as Lancelot du Lac.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the best-known knight of the Round Table.

clue.text: Irrigation of Algarve at regular intervals over time

indicators.note: letters taken at evenly spaced gaps, here every second one, starting from the second

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Farmers in the Algarve water their fields regularly over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: "Over" places AGE after the extracted letters. Lavage is a medical washing out, as of a wound or the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavage is washing out a body cavity, a medical irrigation.

clue.text: Spaniards here competed in scoreless draw

indicators.note: competed goes inside the scoreline

explanation.surface: A Spanish football team plays out a goalless draw.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spaniards" suggests a team, but the definition is a place where Spaniards live: Oviedo, a city in northern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is a Spanish city, a place Spaniards are found.

clue.text: Show without Tarzan struggling to entertain Virginia and Georgia

indicators.note: Tarzan's letters thrash about

parts.note: ex = without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: the rearranged Tarzan holds the two states

explanation.surface: A show goes ahead without its Tarzan, who is busy hosting American guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Ex as a preposition means without, as in ex works price.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with extra colour: the word means a spectacular, lavishly staged entertainment.

clue.text: American not eating in land around Lomé

definitions.meaning: Lomé is the capital of a small West African country

explanation.surface: An American traveller in West Africa who won't eat in the local restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration is (4), so TO GO reads as one word. Americans order food to go where Britons order takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say to go for food not eaten in; Togo is the country whose capital is Lomé.

clue.text: Son leaves belt in corner

indicators.note: the son goes out of the word

explanation.surface: A boy slips out of his belt while in the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: "Corner" looks like a noun; it is the verb, to trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to pin someone where they cannot escape.

clue.text: Excited seeing leg — not small — in flimsy robe

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone is aroused at the sight of a leg in a sheer dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is racy, and the answer belongs in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a flimsy, often sheer, dressing gown.

clue.text: Dance party taking place next to European capital

indicators.note: the party and place follow the capital

explanation.surface: A dance party is being held near a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: "Dance party" looks like one phrase; Dance is the definition and party is DO. A rigadoon is a lively old dance for couples.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively Baroque dance in duple time.
